rewrites.comment: /admin and /admin/login are deliberately NOT prerendered (see src/app/app.routes.server.ts) - they need a live auth check and must never ship pre-baked HTML. Since prerendering now makes '/' resolve to the real, fully-rendered home page file, the generic '**' rewrite below would otherwise serve THAT home-page HTML for an /admin request - a visible flash of the wrong page plus an Angular hydration mismatch, because the router immediately tries to render the Admin component into a DOM tree built for the Home page. index.csr.html is the neutral, un-prerendered app shell Angular generates specifically for Client-render-mode routes; routing admin here first avoids both problems.

A /projects/:id whose id was NOT prerendered (e.g. a project added in Admin after the last deploy) has no static file on disk, so it would otherwise fall through to the generic '**' rewrite below and get served the prerendered HOME page's HTML for that URL - the same hydration-mismatch/content-flash problem as /admin, just for an unbounded set of ids instead of two fixed paths. This only ever applies to an unprerendered id: Firebase Hosting serves a matching static file (e.g. /projects/cJEZ0HL6MYTzD2AbUYat/index.html) directly, without even consulting rewrites, whenever one exists - so a real, already-prerendered project page is unaffected by this rule.

headers.comment: Hashed build assets never change content under the same name, so they can be cached forever.

HTML documents must NOT be cached, or browsers keep serving an old page that points at deleted hashed bundles after a deploy - the classic 'site broken until hard refresh' bug. Before prerendering there was exactly one HTML file (index.html, reused for every route); now there is a real HTML file per page, so every route needs this explicitly - a single '/index.html' rule would not even match a request to '/' under cleanUrls, let alone '/about' or '/projects/<id>'. Split into plain, unambiguous sources (no extglob-in-extglob tricks) so each one is easy to verify by eye.
index.csr.html is the app shell served (via the rewrites above) for /admin and any project id not yet prerendered - same staleness risk as any other HTML document.
SEO files change between deploys; keep them fresh but cacheable for an hour.
Security headers applied to every response.
Force HTTPS for 2 years, including subdomains. Firebase Hosting is HTTPS-only anyway; this stops a downgrade attempt before the first request.
Stops browsers guessing a file is a script when the server said it is not.
Nobody should be able to frame this site - blocks clickjacking of the admin login.
Send the full URL to ourselves, only the origin to third parties, nothing over plain HTTP.
The site needs none of these device APIs; deny them outright.
headers.value: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=(), usb=(), interest-cohort=()

headers.comment: Content-Security-Policy in REPORT-ONLY mode on purpose. It logs violations to the browser console and blocks NOTHING, so it cannot break the site. Watch the console for a week; once it is quiet, rename this header to Content-Security-Policy to start enforcing. Enforcing it blind would almost certainly break Cloudinary images, the Firestore/Storage calls, Google Fonts or Font Awesome.
